response.content:
## AI Companies That Expanded to Norway in 2026

Norway saw a significant wave of AI-related expansion in 2026, driven primarily by demand for AI data center infrastructure and the country's abundant renewable energy. Here are the key companies that expanded into or within Norway:

### Major Expansions

- **OpenAI** — Announced a **Stargate-branded AI data center** in Norway, its first in Europe. The facility, located in Kvanndal near Narvik in northern Norway, is being designed and built by Nscale in partnership with Norwegian energy infrastructure firm Aker. It aims to provide 100,000 NVIDIA GPUs by the end of 2026, with plans to expand significantly.

- **Nscale** (London-based AI infrastructure company) — Massively expanded its presence in Norway, securing **$790 million** in financing (May 2026) for its AI data center campus in **Narvik**, described as the largest AI infrastructure investment in Norway. Nscale also signed a long-term renewable power agreement with Vattenfall for a planned data center in **Kvanndal**, set to commence operations in 2027 with an initial capacity of 230 MW. Total funding exceeded $3.4 billion including a $2 billion Series C round.

- **Google** — Invested approximately **$646 million** to develop its **first data center in Norway**, located in **Skien** (about 50 miles southwest of Oslo). The facility is being built on a 200-hectare site in the Gromstul area, with operations set to commence in 2026.

- **atNorth** (Nordic data center operator) — **Expanded into Norway** in June 2026 with plans to develop a new **mega-site in the Haugaland region** (Gismarvik, on Norway's southwest coast) for AI and high-performance computing. The project is slated to go online in 2028, initially delivering 120 MW and scaling to 350 MW at full capacity.

- **Polar Data Centers** (European AI-ready data center developer) — Announced **DRA02**, a new 40 MW AI-ready data center at its flagship campus in **Drangedal, Norway** (July 2026), as part of its wider European growth strategy.

- **Microsoft** — Identified as having existing and planned data center operations in Norway, with Nscale's Narvik facility reportedly having a multi-year off-take agreement with Microsoft.

- **CoreWeave** and **TikTok** (through Green Mountain) — Also noted as having existing and planned data center presence in Norway.

### Regulatory Context

Norway's rapid AI expansion prompted the government to take action in November 2026. System operator **Statnett** temporarily halted new grid connection applications for data centers, and the government proposed a **licensing system** to prioritize socially beneficial facilities. The moratorium is expected to last until at least August 2027. Existing approved projects are unaffected.

A Norwegian Technology Council report noted that foreign companies own **90% of data center capacity** in Norway, raising questions about the societal benefits of the rapid buildout.

“Data centers are a key infrastructure in our society, but with the pace of development we are seeing now, it becomes necessary to ask the question of scope and how we can align policy so that we get the most out of scarce resources," Tore Tennøe, the board's director, said.

The group, which advises the government as an independent body, plans to release a report later this year with recommendations on regulating the data center sector. [...] # Norway halts grid connection applications for new data centers

Seeks to limit rapid buildout while regulation catches up

The Norwegian government has temporarily halted the reservation of connections for new data centers.

The move effectively acts as a moratorium on new grid-connected data center developments until regulations are in place. Projects already connected or already grid-approved are unaffected.

System operator Statnett AS said that the halt is expected to be lifted no later than Aug. 1, 2027.

“We want data centers in Norway, but we can’t have all types of data centers,” Digitalization Minister Torgeir Micaelsen said.

“We must therefore control the growth and ensure that Norway gets the data centers we actually need — those that provide the greatest societal benefit.”
